title: Video lectures for students on slow networks
summary: Deliver recorded lectures to students on thin data plans without an enormous storage and bandwidth bill.
context: Lalbagh Learning records 500 hours of lectures a week for students across Karnataka. Most watch on phones, often on 3G or a shared data pack, and many watch the night before an exam, all of them the same few videos.
Their storage and bandwidth bill has grown faster than their revenue. Students complain of buffering, and teachers complain when a corrected lecture does not replace the old one.
must_handle: A lecture plays on a poor connection, at a lower quality if need be.
A student can download a lecture and watch it with no connection.
A teacher's correction replaces the old version within an hour.
Old lectures that nobody watches get cheaper to keep.
The night before an exam does not bring the service down.
show_in_answer: The path of a recording from upload to a student's phone.
How videos are stored, and how the cost changes as they age.
What is cached where, and how a correction gets through.
A rough estimate of the monthly storage and bandwidth.
